## Why

The outbound comment sync re-posted duplicate comments to Jira on every hourly pass
(bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` / `aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`: the PRIMARY comment-id dedup map
`comment_ids` is inert/empty, leaving only the lossy body-membership fallback). The
reconcile-bridge workflow is **paused** (`disabled_manually`, confirmed via the Actions API),
so the duplicate set is FIXED and no longer growing. **REB-1861** is pinned at Jira's
5000-comment HARD cap, so new comments on it fail with `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.
This ticket purges the accumulated duplicates.

Same failure class, different route, as bug `1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356`; its cleanup task
`bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` is the established precedent, whose mechanism is reused here.

## How the affected-issue set is enumerated (deterministic, not a guess)

The set is derived from the LAST reconcile pass before the pause — Actions run **32403944666** of
`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` (2026-08-20T18:34Z). Every touched issue emits
`RECON: outbound_update key=<KEY> changed=[...] comments=<N>`; the affected set is exactly the keys
with `comments>0`. Reproduce with:

```
gh run view 32403944666 --log \
  | grep -oE "RECON: outbound_update key=[A-Z]+-[0-9]+ changed=\[[^]]*\] comments=[0-9]+" \
  | sed -E 's/.*key=([A-Z]+-[0-9]+).*comments=([0-9]+)/\1 \2/' | awk '$2>0'
```

That yields **30 issues** (the bug ticket's "~28" estimate). Keys with `comments=0` in that pass
are converged and cannot be carrying duplicates from this bug: the body-membership fallback is
deterministic, so an issue that matches today matched on every prior pass. The enumerated list is
the completeness baseline for the run, is written to an artifact, and drives the script; the
run is REFUSED if the key list and the artifact disagree.

Measured damage (read-only dry run over that list; all 30 passed the completeness check):

The full 30-row per-issue table (Jira total / unmarked / distinct bodies / duplicates) is recorded
as a comment on this ticket and in artifact `logs/dryrun-all.txt`.

**Totals: 31,683 Jira comments; 30,847 bot-marked; 836 unmarked; 836 distinct bodies kept;
30,011 duplicates to delete.**

## Mechanism (reused from bd80 — see that ticket for the full rationale)

- **Bot identification — the safety-critical filter. Marker detection runs on the PRE-STRIP
  rendered text.** A comment is a deletion candidate IFF
  `adf.adf_to_text(comment["body"])` — the raw ADF→text render, with NO marker strip — contains
  `RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"` (`outbound_comments.py`, appended by
  `_decorate_outbound_comment`). This is deliberately NOT `_normalize_comment_body`, which
  STRIPS the marker before returning and therefore can never be used for detection. The two uses
  are kept separate and explicit:
  *detection* = `adf.adf_to_text(body)` (pre-strip);
  *dedup grouping* = `_normalize_comment_body(body)` (post-strip).
  A comment whose pre-strip rendered text lacks the marker is treated as foreign and is NEVER a
  deletion candidate in phase 1.
- **Secondary cross-check.** All candidates on an issue must resolve to a single bot `author.accountId`; divergence aborts that issue. Observed homogeneous: `712020:6471376f-4e5e-4ed2-8c05-330827bc387e` (the accountId bd80 recorded).
- **Dedup key = the reconciler's OWN normalization.** Group candidates by
  `outbound_comments._normalize_comment_body(body)`, imported and reused verbatim, so "distinct
  body" means exactly what the reconciler means by it.
- **Keep-one rule.** Per distinct normalized body: keep the OLDEST copy (min `created`), delete
  the rest. A body with only ONE copy is NEVER deleted. This structurally guarantees the
  invariant that every distinct body retains exactly one instance.
- **Pagination + completeness gate.** All comments are fetched via
  `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment?startAt=..&maxResults=100&orderBy=created` and the count
  is reconciled against the `total` from `?maxResults=0`. `len(fetched) != total` REFUSES that
  issue (guards a silently truncated fetch producing a dangerous delete list).
- **Rate limiting — 429 IS retried, explicitly.** DELETE does NOT go through
  `delete_comment`/`_direct_rest_delete`, which re-raise 4xx/5xx immediately and would hard-abort
  on the first 429 across ~30k calls. Every request goes through the script's own wrapper, which
  honours `Retry-After` on 429 and backs off exponentially on 5xx/transient faults, plus a
  per-call throttle. A 404 on DELETE is idempotent success, so re-runs are safe.
- **Append-only deletion log** (`logs/deletions.jsonl`: key, id, body hash, outcome, ts) flushed per deletion, so a stalled run is resumable.

### Phase 2 — the 836 truncation-suffix comments (separate, evidence-gated)

Three issues (REB-1567: 418, REB-1931: 278, REB-2605: 140) carry comments with NO marker. They are
not human: same bot accountId, repeated ~139x identically, rendered text ending in
`_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = " … [truncated by reconciler]"` (`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`) — the
reconciler's own outbound truncation, which cut the 32767-char body short and removed the trailing
marker paragraph. Because the phase-1 authoritative identifier is absent, these run as a SEPARATE
phase behind `--include-truncated`, with its own dry run, under the rule: rendered text ends with
`_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` AND `author.accountId` == the resolved bot accountId. Keep-one still applies,
so the one-surviving-copy invariant is unchanged. Phase 2 is not needed to clear the cap.

## Safety plan (T4 — irreversible)

- [ ] **Pre-deletion backup** of the FULL comment payload (id, ADF body, author accountId +
      display name, created) per issue, written and completeness-checked BEFORE any DELETE.
- [ ] **Dry-run default.** Deletion requires an explicit `--execute`. The dry run prints, per
      issue: fetched/reported total, marked count, unmarked count, distinct-body count, the kept
      id per body, and the delete count, and writes a per-issue machine-readable plan artifact.
- [ ] **Canary first.** Execute on ONE light issue, verify it fully, then proceed.
      **REB-1861 runs LAST** (largest and riskiest).
- [ ] **Per-issue post-verification**: re-fetch and assert every distinct normalized body present
      before the run still has exactly one surviving copy, that the unmarked count is unchanged,
      and that the issue is below the cap.
- [ ] Ambiguous cases are SKIPPED and reported, never guessed.
- [ ] The reconcile-bridge workflow stays PAUSED for the whole operation and is NOT re-enabled
      by this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The affected-issue list is derived by the documented command from run 32403944666, written
      as an artifact, and the executed run covers exactly that list (30 issues). Proving command:
      the enumeration command above; the script's per-issue summary lists the same keys.
- [ ] Per issue, `len(fetched) == total` from `?maxResults=0` holds and a backup artifact exists
      BEFORE any DELETE; a mismatch refuses that issue with no DELETE issued.
- [ ] Dry-run output is produced and inspected before `--execute`.
- [ ] Marker detection is on the PRE-STRIP rendered text (`adf.adf_to_text`); post-strip
      `_normalize_comment_body` is used only for dedup grouping. Proving command: the dry run
      reports non-zero `marked` counts — detection on stripped text would report 0.
- [ ] Every DELETE routes through a wrapper that honours `Retry-After` on HTTP 429 and retries
      5xx/transient faults; a 429 does not abort the run.
- [ ] After the run every issue is below the 5000 cap, and REB-1861 drops from 5000 to its
      distinct-body count.
- [ ] For every issue touched, a post-deletion re-fetch confirms zero missing distinct bodies and
      an unchanged unmarked count (zero content loss, no human comment deleted).
- [ ] A deletion log with one JSON object per deletion exists for the executed run; its line count
      matches the reported delete count.
